updates.title: AWS adds domain and location controls to Bedrock Web Search
updates.whatChanged: AWS adds two optional controls to Amazon Bedrock Web Search on 23 October. The `web_search` tool accepts up to 100 allowed or blocked domains and optional user-location parameters in existing OpenAI Responses API requests. The controls are available in three commercial US Regions and AWS GovCloud (US-West).
updates.whyCare: You can constrain grounded answers to approved domains and tailor location-sensitive searches without a separate search connector. Check regional availability and page-fetch permissions before you rely on results.
updates.before: Bedrock Web Search could ground Responses API answers, but it had no domain filters or user-location controls.
updates.after: `web_search` accepts up to 100 allowed or blocked domains and optional user-location parameters in four supported AWS Regions.
updates.learn: Test allowlists and blocklists against your source policy. Check region support and set IAM permissions and `external_web_access` to match your fetch requirements.

updates.architectureImplication: Use Bedrock Web Search when its indexed sources and four US Regions fit your requirements. Keep a separate search connector for other regions or custom retrieval behavior, and set fetch permissions to match your data boundary.
